svg.text: Inside a fire bay: front-line trench cross-section (3D)
Original illustrative diagram of a typical British fire trench, about 1916–17. Proportions approximate; 1 grid square = 1 m.
sandbags and earth on the enemy side;
stops bullets, about 1.5 m above the fire-step
raised rear bank: protects against blast
from behind and avoids skylining heads
a ledge ~0.6–0.9 m high; men stood
here to fire over the parapet
timber, wire mesh or corrugated iron
small shelter scraped into the wall
earth block at each end of the bay;
contains blast and stops enfilade fire
belts several metres deep in front
lets a sentry look out without exposing his head
with a rifle resting on the parapet
